::: {#exr-golden-ratio}
## The golden ratio

::: {.lm-solution}
1. With $F_1, \ldots, F_6 = 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8$: $q_1 = 1$, $q_2 = 2$, $q_3 = 3/2$, $q_4 = 5/3$, $q_5 = 8/5$.

1. Dividing $F_{n+2} = F_{n+1} + F_n$ by $F_{n+1}$ gives $q_{n+1} = 1 + F_n / F_{n+1} = 1 + 1 / q_n$.

1. For the limit $q$, $q = 1 + 1/q$, so $q^2 - q - 1 = 0$. Since all $q_n \geq 1$, the limit is the positive root, the golden ratio
   $$
     \varphi = \frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2} \approx 1.618.
   $$
:::
:::

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
fibonacci <- read.csv("data/fibonacci.csv")
```

::: {#exr-fibonacci}
## How fast do the ratios converge?

### Implementation

::: {.lm-solution}
```{r}
fibonacci_ratios <- function(F) {
  F[-1] / F[-length(F)]
}

fibonacci_ratios(c(1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8))
```
:::

### Errors

::: {.lm-solution}
```{r}
fibonacci$q <- c(fibonacci_ratios(fibonacci$F), NA)
fibonacci$error <- abs(fibonacci$q - (1 + sqrt(5)) / 2)
head(fibonacci, 20)
```

The error falls by the factor $\varphi^2 \approx 2.6$ in each step: the ratios lie alternately above and below $\varphi$, closer each time.
:::
:::
